note: Round-20 precision suite, assembled by assemble-suite.py from .ufo/waves/round-20/w1/cases/<seat>/ (wave-1 case authors, blind to the repaired tool). Counter: tw-precision.py. `before` is the author's reading, re-measured by the counter. Set: scored

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-frozenset-closure
cases.why: The exact rejected-harm counterexample stores argv strings in a frozenset and must be clean.

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-frozenset-direct
cases.why: A builtin frozenset call only constructs a pure value from the literal list.

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-type-list
cases.why: The builtin type inspects the list value and does not execute its contents.

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-bool-list
cases.why: The builtin bool tests the list value without dispatching its string elements.

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-callable-list
cases.why: The builtin callable inspects whether the supplied list is callable and cannot spawn argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-ascii-list
cases.why: The builtin ascii formats the literal list as text and does not run it.

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-format-list
cases.why: The builtin format returns a textual representation of the supplied list.

cases.name: P-CasePureBuiltins-str-control
cases.why: The existing PURE_ARG_CALLS exemption keeps a direct str formatting call clean.

cases.name: P-CasePureCollections-deque
cases.why: A collections deque stores a literal package-query argv as inert data.

cases.name: P-CasePureCollections-counter
cases.why: A collections Counter counts literal command tokens without invoking them.

cases.name: P-CasePureCollections-namedtuple-instance
cases.why: A namedtuple instance stores literal argv in a record field without spawning it.

cases.name: P-CasePureCollections-typing-namedtuple
cases.why: An instance of a visible typing.NamedTuple class stores literal argv as data.

cases.name: P-CasePureCollections-mapping-containers
cases.why: OrderedDict, defaultdict(list), and ChainMap organize a literal argv without spawning it.

cases.name: P-CasePureCollections-module-alias-control
cases.why: collections attribute constructors are a clean module-alias control for argv data.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-shlex-join
cases.why: shlex.join imported by name only renders the sudo pacman -S argv as one quoted string; nothing spawns it.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-json-dumps
cases.why: json.dumps imported by name serializes the systemctl restart argv to JSON text; nothing spawns it.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-pprint-pformat
cases.why: pprint.pformat imported by name pretty-prints the pacman -Q argv; nothing spawns it.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-textwrap-indent-chain
cases.why: Two same-text defs (block -> line, depth 2) only join and textwrap.indent the systemctl restart argv; no body spawns.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-lambda-join
cases.why: A same-text lambda whose visible body is ' '.join(argv) only formats the sudo pacman -S argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-fstring-def
cases.why: A same-text def returns an f-string around shlex.join(argv) for the pacman -Q argv; its visible body spawns nothing.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-str-format-bound
cases.why: A name bound to a str literal's .format method only renders the systemctl restart argv as text.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-quote-cross-cell
cases.why: A def in an earlier py cell (no reset) shell-quotes each token with shlex.quote; the later call only formats the sudo pacman -S argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-dumps-alias
cases.why: json.dumps imported under an alias (from json import dumps as to_json) only serializes the sudo pacman -S argv; the alias binds a pure stdlib callable.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-join-cross-cell-import
cases.why: shlex.join imported in an earlier py cell (no reset) is the binding in effect at the later call, which only renders the pacman -Q argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-partial-dumps
cases.why: functools.partial over json.dumps (not over a spawn) is a configured formatter; calling it on the systemctl restart argv only serializes it.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-fstring-def-control
cases.why: Control: a same-text def returning an f-string over ' '.join(argv) is already resolved and clean at both baselines; it must stay clean.

cases.name: P-CasePureFormatters-dotted-control
cases.why: Control: module-qualified attribute formatters (shlex.join, json.dumps, pprint.pformat, textwrap.indent) are unflagged at both baselines and must stay clean.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-dataclass-ctor
cases.why: A same-cell @dataclass Case only stores the sudo pacman argv as a field; its generated __init__ cannot spawn.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-plain-class-init
cases.why: A same-cell plain class whose __init__ only assigns attributes stores the pacman argv as data.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-functools-cache-def
cases.why: A @functools.cache def whose visible body only joins the argv tuple into text; decorated, still pure.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-async-def-await
cases.why: An awaited same-cell async def whose visible body only prints the argv list.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-duplicate-def
cases.why: Two printing defs of one name: the binding in effect at the call (the second) only prints the argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-duplicate-def-later-spawner
cases.why: The pure first def is the binding in effect at the call; a spawning redefinition only follows the call.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-duplicate-def-earlier-spawner
cases.why: A spawning def is rebound by a printing def before the call; the latest preceding binding only prints.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-nested-def
cases.why: A def nested inside the calling def has a visible print-only body; the literal argv is never spawned.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-nested-def-param
cases.why: A nested formatting def receives an argv completed by the enclosing helper's literal parameter; nothing spawns.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-lambda-same-cell
cases.why: A same-cell lambda bound to fmt only joins the systemctl argv into a string for print.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-transitive-class
cases.why: A visible def hands its argv to a visible class whose __init__ only joins it: pure at depth two.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-same-text-decorator
cases.why: A def wrapped by a visible same-cell logging decorator: wrapper and body only print and join the git argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-staticmethod-classmethod-control
cases.why: Control: staticmethod/classmethod formatters on a same-cell class are attribute calls and stay unflagged.

cases.name: P-CasePureCallables-two-hop-plain-control
cases.why: Control: two plain same-cell defs, resolved by literal binding, only format and print the argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureCrossCell-write-case
cases.why: A visible prior-cell helper serializes literal command-looking argv as data and never spawns it.

cases.name: P-CasePureCrossCell-expect-case
cases.why: A visible prior-cell assertion helper only compares literal argv data.

cases.name: P-CasePureCrossCell-dataclass-case
cases.why: A prior-cell dataclass constructor stores command-looking argv as tuple data.

cases.name: P-CasePureCrossCell-namedtuple-class-case
cases.why: A prior-cell NamedTuple class constructs a record holding command-looking argv without execution.

cases.name: P-CasePureCrossCell-namedtuple-factory-case
cases.why: A prior-cell collections.namedtuple factory creates a data record with command-looking argv.

cases.name: P-CasePureCrossCell-lambda-format-case
cases.why: A prior-cell lambda passes literal argv only to json.dumps for formatting.

cases.name: L-CasePureCrossCell-reset-clears-helper
cases.why: A reset discards the visible pure helper before a literal argv call, which must remain a lead.

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-print-lambda-spawn
cases.why: print is rebound by assignment to a visible lambda whose body spawns its argv, so the builtin exemption is lost and the call is observed (E1 lambda helper, E3 assignment).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-print-imported
cases.why: print is rebound by an import from a module outside the known-pure stdlib set; its body is not visible, so the literal argv is a lead (E1 lead, E3 import).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-list-bound-to-spawn
cases.why: list is rebound by assignment to subprocess.run, a spawn alias bound in the text, so list([...]) is an observed spawn, not a pure builtin call (E1 alias, E3 assignment).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-frozenset-def-spawn
cases.why: Control: the round-19 BLOCK=frozenset([...]) shape after def frozenset rebinds the builtin to a visible spawner; the E2 frozenset exemption must not swallow it (E3 def).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-run-redef-pure
cases.why: The latest preceding binding of run is a visible def that only joins its argv; the earlier spawner def is no longer in effect at the call (E3 latest binding, E2 pure def).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-run-call-before-spawn-redef
cases.why: At the call the binding in effect is the pure join def; the spawner def that follows rebinds run only after the call and its body has no literal argv (E3 preceding binding).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-run-import-rebound-print
cases.why: Dry-run toggle: the subprocess.run alias is rebound to builtin print before the call, so the call prints the argv and spawns nothing (E3 assignment over import, E2 builtin).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-run-redef-cross-cell
cases.why: Across cells with no reset the latest preceding binding of run is cell 2's pure join def, not cell 1's spawner (E3 across earlier cells, E2 pure def).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-print-def-cross-cell
cases.why: Cell 1 rebinds builtin print to a visible spawner def and no reset follows, so cell 2's print([...]) is an observed spawn (E1 earlier-cell helper, E3 def).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-del-run
cases.why: del run unbinds the visible spawner, so the later run([...]) names an unbound bare name whose body is not visible: a lead, not observed (E3 del, E1 lead).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-del-run-cross-cell
cases.why: A del in an intervening cell unbinds cell 1's spawner for later cells; cell 3's run([...]) is an unbound bare name, a lead (E3 del carried across cells).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-del-print-restores-builtin
cases.why: After del print at module scope the name resolves to builtins.print again (CPython executionmodel: global, then builtins), so the call is the pure builtin: no row; evidence-fixed against E3's literal 'then a lead' (E2).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-param-shadows-helper
cases.why: Inside preview, run is the parameter, which shadows the module spawner def; it is bound only to the imported show, whose body is not visible, so the argv is a lead (E3 scope).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-param-shadows-spawn-alias
cases.why: The parameter run shadows the from-subprocess alias inside preview and is bound only to the imported show, so the literal argv is a lead, not an observed spawn (E3 scope).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-shlex-join-as-run
cases.why: run is bound by import alias to shlex.join, a known-pure stdlib formatter, so run([...]) only builds a string (E2 shlex.join, E3 import alias).

cases.name: S-CaseShadowing-run-as-frozenset-control
cases.why: Control: frozenset is bound by from subprocess import run as frozenset, a spawn alias, so the round-19 BLOCK shape here really spawns and stays observed (E1 alias, E3 import).

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-r13-shape
cases.why: control: round-13 run_record(name, argv, rc, **kw) body is visible in line 1 (earlier py cell, no reset) and its literal argv reaches subprocess.run, so line 2 is observed, never lead

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-r13-verbatim
cases.why: control: verbatim MadoR13.jsonl:437 def (literal defaults, runs then records) + :470 call that frozen r13-root.jsonl:4 keeps without its def; with the def visible the pacman -Q call is observed

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-kw-argv
cases.why: keyword argv= to the line-1 wrapper: rule B reads positional lists only, so 1f7f995 misses it; the visible body binds argv and spawns it, observed

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-check-true
cases.why: line-1 wrapper with a check=True kwarg, called on line 2 with keywords only (check=True, plus timeout= that lands in **kw); the bound argv reaches subprocess.run, so sudo pacman -S is observed

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-two-hop
cases.why: two hops across cells: pkg_version (line 2) builds the argv from its parameter and hands it to run_record (line 1); the literal call on line 3 reaches subprocess.run, observed there

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-format-then-run
cases.why: line-1 helper formats the command line from literal parts, prints it, then runs it with shell=True; the line-2 call states every part, so pacman -Qi is observed

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-gap-cell
cases.why: helper defined on line 1, unrelated non-reset py cell on line 2, literal call on line 3: the kernel keeps the def, so pacman -Ql is observed on line 3

cases.name: W-WrapperCrossCell-git-commit
cases.why: line-1 helper runs git add then git commit with its bound parameters; the literal line-2 call makes both writes observed (string arguments, so rule B never fired)

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-spawn-kwarg-args
cases.why: A literal spawn whose argv is stated by keyword (args=[...]); both tools read only node.args[0], so the spawn is counted unparsed and missed.

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-alias-assign-shell
cases.why: run = subprocess.run binds a spawn alias in the text (E1), so run('pacman -Qi hyprland', shell=True) is a literal spawn; neither tool resolves assignment aliases and rule B reads only argv lists (silent: unparsed_spawns 0).

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-partial-shell-sudo
cases.why: functools.partial(subprocess.run, shell=True, check=True) is a spawn alias (E1); the literal sudo pacman -S string handed to it is missed silently (unparsed_spawns 0) by both tools.

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-decorated-cache-param
cases.why: @functools.cache removes a visible spawning def from same-text helper resolution (decorator_list check), so pkg_version('hyprland') never reaches ['pacman','-Q',name]; the undecorated twin resolves at 1f7f995.

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-decorated-lrucache-call
cases.why: Same miss with the Call-decorator shape the real corpus uses (lru_cache(...)); guards resolution that is agnostic to the decorator's AST shape.

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-async-def-exec-param
cases.why: An async def helper (AsyncFunctionDef is not a resolvable helper) feeds its literal argument into asyncio.create_subprocess_exec('pacman','-Q',name); the exec is counted unparsed and missed.

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-lambda-param-argv
cases.why: A lambda spawner bound by assignment is not a resolvable helper and its literal str argument is not an argv list, so rule B is silent and the body spawn is unparsed.

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-class-method-instance
cases.why: Control, stated miss: Runner().run([...]) is a method call through an instance; E1 lists def/async def/lambda helpers only and E2 keeps attribute/method calls unflagged, so it stays clean (unparsed_spawns 1); resolving it later needs a case edit with reason.

cases.name: W-CaseWrapperForms-async-def-exec-starred
cases.why: Control: 1f7f995 passes only through rule B's unmarked bare-name row; the target must keep it observed by folding create_subprocess_exec(*argv) in the visible async body, not demote it to lead or drop it.

cases.name: H-HelpBash-jj-st-h

cases.name: H-HelpBash-jj-git-push-help

cases.name: H-HelpBash-git-commit-h

cases.name: H-HelpBash-git-help-flag-commit
cases.why: red: `git --help commit` runs `git help commit` (man page); git 2.56.0 rc=0, HEAD and .git tree unchanged; 1f7f995 skips the flag and flags git:commit

cases.name: H-HelpBash-git-stash-h
cases.why: red: -h prints stash usage and stashes nothing; git 2.56.0 rc=0, stash list 0->0, tree unchanged (plain `git stash` 0->1); 1f7f995 flags git:stash

cases.name: H-HelpBash-git-commit-m-x-help
cases.why: red: a later --help still stops git commit at option parsing (usage); git 2.56.0 rc=0, HEAD and .git tree unchanged with staged changes; 1f7f995 flags git:commit

cases.name: H-HelpBash-jj-help-commit

cases.name: H-HelpBash-git-help-push

cases.name: H-HelpBash-git-commit-m-help

cases.name: H-HelpBash-jj-help-then-describe
cases.why: write negative: a help segment then a real describe; jj 0.45.1 op log 6->8, description ''->'x'; exactly one jj:describe row (1f7f995 keeps only the help segment's row, deduped)

cases.name: H-HelpBash-jj-st-h-then-describe

cases.name: H-HelpBash-jj-describe-message-eq-help

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-commit-dry-run
cases.why: git commit --dry-run only shows what would be committed: /tmp repro kept HEAD, refs and staged entries and ran no hook (it did write the would-be tree and index cache-tree).

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-add-n
cases.why: add -n is --dry-run per `git add -h`; /tmp repro left index bytes and objects identical.

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-add-dry-run
cases.why: git add --dry-run lists what would be added; /tmp repro left index bytes and objects identical.

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-push-n-origin-master
cases.why: push -n is --dry-run per `git push -h`; bare /tmp remote refs and tracking refs unchanged.

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-push-dry-run
cases.why: git push --dry-run to the upstream; bare /tmp remote refs and tracking refs unchanged.

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-push-trailing-dry-run
cases.why: git accepts the flag after the refspec (a flag-position check); /tmp remote unchanged.

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-jj-push-dry-run-ignore-wc
cases.why: No snapshot and no push: /tmp colocated repro with a dirty working copy kept op heads, git refs/index and the remote unchanged.

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-jj-push-dry-run-snapshots

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-commit-n-no-verify
cases.why: On commit -n is --no-verify: /tmp repro created the commit and skipped the pre-commit/commit-msg hooks.

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-add-n-then-add
cases.why: A dry run followed by a real add in the same text: exactly one git:add row (the real one).

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-push-dry-run-then-push

cases.name: H-CaseDryRunBash-commit-msg-value-dry-run

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-run-add-n

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-bang-jj-help-flags

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-check-output-help-before-sub

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-popen-push-dry-runs

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-helper-commit-h-late-help

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-tool-bash-jj-commit-help
cases.why: tool.bash spawn of jj commit --help: help flag, no snapshot (E4); measured jj 0.45.1 dirty working copy: ops +0

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-ctl-dry-then-push-same-cell

cases.name: H-CaseHelpDryRunEval-ctl-commit-m-dry-run-value

cases.name: L-CaseLeadsInvisible-run-record
cases.why: An undefined bare helper receives the literal pacman query argv; the transcript does not show whether run_record executes it.

cases.name: L-CaseLeadsInvisible-import-run-cmd
cases.why: The non-pure imported run_cmd body is outside this transcript, so the stated sudo pacman argv is a lead rather than observed execution.

cases.name: L-CaseLeadsInvisible-import-classify-argv
cases.why: The assertion only consumes an imported classifier's result; with its body invisible, passing the literal argv is not evidence that the command ran.

cases.name: L-CaseLeadsInvisible-opaque-runner
cases.why: The local run binding comes from opaque make_runner(), so the literal argv is a lead and its execution path is not visible.

cases.name: L-CaseLeadsInvisible-reset-cleared-helper
cases.why: The reset on the second eval cell clears the earlier run_record definition; the later literal argv has no visible helper body.

cases.name: L-CaseLeadsInvisible-import-alias
cases.why: The imported launch alias has no visible body; passing a literal sudo pacman argv warrants lead rows, not observed execution.

cases.name: P-AdoptW2-CriticC3W2-dc-dataclass
cases.why: E2: same-text @dataclass Case has no spawn in its body; the ctor only stores the argv
